sanity_expectations: f is non-negative everywhere in the sampled region
At fixed T=Topt, f rises steeply from ~0 at low R and saturates toward a plateau (Holling type-II / accelerating-then-saturating shape)
f -> 0 as R -> 0 (low-density accessibility cutoff via 1 - exp(-R/P))
Along T at fixed R, f peaks at T=Topt=25 and falls off symmetrically (Gaussian thermal-performance curve)
At high prey density (R >> Rc=20), intake is depressed by the refuge factor toward (1-g)=~0.5 of the un-suppressed level, so the high-R plateau sits below the parent's plateau
f is bounded above by 1/Th = 5 times the modifier factors (well under ~2.6 at the sampled optimum)
excitation_report: Explicit expression is a single multiplicative product; as one additive term its RMS reaches 33.7*sigma over R in [0.5,50], T in [10,35] (sigma=0.05). NEW term = full expression minus parent, i.e. the refuge/aggregation factor (1 - g/(1 + (Rc/R)^m)): peak effect 2.08, sigma_multiple 41.5, strongest at R≈48.8, T≈25.6 — as expected the suppression bites at high prey density where R exceeds Rc=20. All terms visible; no weak terms.
role_corrections: f: O->O (confirmed: explicit LHS output, solvable for target, not present on RHS)
R: V->V (confirmed: prey density, primary sampling axis; differentiated axis of the functional response)
T: V->V (confirmed: enclosure temperature, secondary sampling axis of thermal-performance modifier)
P: P->P (confirmed: low-density detectability threshold, fixed)
g: P->P (confirmed: max refuge suppression fraction, fixed)
Rc: P->P (confirmed: half-saturation density of refuge onset, fixed)
rationale: Structural analysis (analyze_expression) shows an explicit, target-solvable relation with no derivatives or integral kernels, so equation_type=explicit and integrator=evaluate_explicit. f is the determined output; R (prey density) and T (temperature) are the two natural sampling axes and get ranges; all remaining symbols are fixed parameters. Ranges: R in [0.5,50] spans the low-density rise, the Holling saturation, and crucially crosses Rc=20 so the new refuge term is excited; T in [10,35] straddles Topt=25 to exercise the thermal Gaussian. Parameter magnitudes chosen for a plausible type-II functional response (max intake 1/Th=5) with a mild density exponent, moderate satiation, low-density cutoff at P=2, thermal width b=0.01, and the suggested refuge magnitudes (g=0.5 in [0,0.8], Rc=20 in [1,50], m=3 in [1,6]). check_substitution at (R=10,T=25) gives finite real f=2.54; excitation_check confirms every term and the new refuge term exceed 5*sigma with sigma=0.05.

scenario_text: A predator consumes prey whose availability varies across experimental enclosures. At low prey density the predator's intake rises steeply, but handling and processing time cause intake to level off as prey become abundant. Each enclosure provides an independent measurement of per-predator consumption at a fixed prey density. The aim is to describe how individual feeding rate depends on prey density.
